newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures off on NY, weak Tankan rumour.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures off on NY, weak Tankan rumour.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures slipped through technical support on Tuesday morning after a sharp fall on Wall Street and amid rumours that the Bank of Japan survey of corporate sentiment would be more bearish than expected.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 192 points overnight to 7,604 in its second largest single-day drop ever. The fall followed comments by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto about potential sales of U.S. Treasures by Japan.

Those comments, combined with rumours that the BOJ's Tankan report on Wednesday might show a bearish Japanese corporate outlook, pushed the Nikkei 225 September futures contract down through chart support at 20,300/400.
By the lunchtime close, the September contract stood at 20,235, down 175 overall.
"The market is still well above 20,000 points but I think it will move a little bit lower, to try the 20,060/70 range, before recovering," said a Singapore-based trader.
The June MSCI Taiwan index contract also weakened, falling 3.2 points to 378.8 on 455 lots by 0300 GMT.
